key_insight: Data-center workload flexibility becomes electrically usable only when scheduling respects converter and network operating limits.
engineering_relevance: Coordinating computing demand with photovoltaic generation, storage, and grid purchases can reduce grid dependence without compromising electrical feasibility.
method: Model training tasks with mixed-integer constraints preserving synchronous configurations and completion requirements.
Aggregate inference flexibility using Minkowski sums and Shapley–Folkman convexification.
Coordinate workloads and energy resources through a four-node electrical model with second-order cone relaxation.
evidence_signal: Case studies report negligible inference shortage with coordinated scheduling and verification against the original AC model, while fixed training cannot support full inference service within voltage limits under the studied conditions.
watch_item: The inference relaxation-gap bound is conditional, and deployments should verify relaxed schedules against their actual electrical networks.
paper_title: Converter-Aware Coordination of Computing Flexibility in Behind-the-Meter Data Centers
